$schema_note: Forge Lexicon v1.0.5 — canonical mapping from internal (lineage) vocabulary to public-surface vocabulary. Consumed by: translation passes, term-leak linter, lineage document. This file is itself a public artifact; it contains no secrets, only naming policy.

brand.policy: The public brand is 'Solomon's Forge', admitted as a scoped exception via brand_allowlist below. The brand is a label, never technical vocabulary: specifications refer to 'the Forge handoff contract', 'Forge core invariants'. 'Solomon's Key' is the public name of the Key verifier (https://github.com/SnakeWard/solomons-key), Forge's verification layer, published by Little Revelations Studio. Forge may link to it and name it; the full name is admitted only through brand_allowlist, and technical prose uses 'Key'.
brand.rationale: Evocative brands on rigorously plain engineering are industry-normal (Prometheus, Kafka, Kubernetes). The brand exception is mechanically scoped: the exact string is permitted only in designated files; all other occurrences of the pattern remain violations.

brand_allowlist.rule: In allowed_files only, each exact occurrence of an allowed string is removed from a line before pattern matching. All other matches, in any file, remain violations. The allowlist never applies to spec/**, src/**, examples/**, or test/**. Since 1.0.5 the allowed strings also include the Key verifier's name and its published attestation log command name (sk-ledger), which contains a word this lexicon otherwise maps; they are exact external identifiers, not Forge vocabulary.

scopes.public_surface: Everything in the repository except excluded_paths: README, specifications, code identifiers, examples, tests, CI config, package metadata, published docs
scopes.internal_only: Lineage document, private build notes, pass reports on the private side, conversation shorthand

entries.public_term: Solomon's Forge (brand, allowlisted files only) / Forge (in technical prose)
entries.notes: Pattern still catches any 'Solomon' variant; the brand_allowlist carves the sole exception. Bare 'Solomon' is a violation everywhere, including allowlisted files.

entries.public_term: Key (the Key verifier, Forge's verification layer; separate repository)
entries.notes: Since 1.0.5 no longer reserved: the name belongs to the Key verifier at https://github.com/SnakeWard/solomons-key. Covered by the Solomon pattern above; the full name is admitted through brand_allowlist in listed files only. Technical prose and specifications say 'Key'.

Industry-standard term for a declarative file a runtime validates and executes. File naming convention on public surface: *.manifest.yaml. Bare word 'key' is NOT linted (too common); only the compound forms are. Since 1.0.5: the Key verifier names its own contract files with this suffix. That naming lives in the Key repository and is outside this scan. Decision: Forge files do not use the suffix; Forge names its Key contract key-contract.yaml, and the pattern stays active to keep the retired term off Forge's public surface.
Describes function rather than asserting it. 'Runtime' alone is acceptable where context is unambiguous.
HIGHEST-PRIORITY translation; most lore-dependent term. Long form where precision matters: 'deterministic tool contract'. Code identifiers: sealedTool / SealedTool.
Covered by Hollow patterns above. 'Local execution shim' or 'simulated service layer' are both acceptable.
Standard compiler vocabulary for sixty years.
CI/CD-native term. Fail-closed semantics stated explicitly in specs.

'Invariant' = a property that must hold at all times. 'Doctrine lock' becomes 'invariant lock'. Since 1.0.5: the Key verifier's README uses this word for Forge's core invariants; alignment is tracked as a Key dependency in docs/roadmap/README.md.

Deliberately aligned with in-toto/SLSA vocabulary. Retains append-only, PROV-O-mapped semantics. Since 1.0.5: the Key verifier's command names contain this word; the hyphenated name sk-ledger is admitted through brand_allowlist (the underscore form sk_ledger never matches the pattern). Key's own prose still uses the word; aligning the two vocabularies is tracked as a Key dependency in docs/roadmap/README.md.
Zero-translation-burden standard term. 'LOT route' becomes 'route'.
'Verification level' is self-describing and echoes SLSA levels.
Already professional engineering vocabulary. Flagship named mechanism.
In prose, 'low-quality output' or 'defect' replaces 'slop'.

entries.internal_term: Witness (the ledger serves as the witness)
entries.notes: Public phrasing: 'the log attests'.
Public phrasing: 'tests validate'. Narrow pattern to avoid false positives.
Plain-English rule kept in informal prose; formal spec sections use 'completion verification'. Not linted.
Already plain English. Flagship export.
Standard industry term. The handoff contract is the first public deliverable.
Covered by Hollow patterns.

entries.public_term: (internal project name — not on public surface in v1)
entries.notes: The orchestration system remains private in v1. Revisit when/if the runtime is published.

linter_policy.match_mode: regex, word-boundary, case-sensitive as written per pattern
linter_policy.on_hit: fail CI with file, line, matched pattern, and suggested public term
linter_policy.policy_note: v1.0.3 inverts coverage: everything is scanned except narrow exclusions. This closes the recurring class of gap where new directories (.github, test, examples) were silently unscanned. v1.0.4 excludes docs/case-study-gates.md: an incident record that quotes rule violations verbatim as evidence, per the same rationale as LINEAGE.md. v1.0.5 records 'Solomon's Key' as the name of the Key verifier (Forge's verification layer) instead of a reserved name, admits that name and Key's attestation log command name sk-ledger through brand_allowlist, extends allowed_files to docs/roadmap/README.md, and records that Forge files do not use the Key contract file suffix.
linter_policy.known_false_positive_guidance: The words 'key', 'judge', 'pass', 'gate' in ordinary English are permitted; only the compound/branded patterns listed above are violations.

lineage_policy.purpose: Records the original vocabulary, the mapping in this file, why the names existed, and how the Key name moved from reserved to the name of the Key verifier.
lineage_policy.rule: Lineage is culture, not interface. It never leads public documents and is never required reading to evaluate the framework.
